name: California
summary: Statutes and constitution: the official Legislative Counsel site (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and failed every WebFetch, so the working routes are tier 2. california.public.law has constructible per-section URLs for all 29 codes (shell and WebFetch both work). Justia covers the codes and the constitution, reached by index navigation. Rules of Court: courts.ca.gov/cms/rules is constructible and fetchable. Case law: the courts.ca.gov opinion listings (120-day slip window plus an older-than-120-days archive) can be fetched, but the opinion PDFs redirect to www4.courts.ca.gov, which is Cloudflare-challenged and robots-refused to WebFetch. The Official Reports (LexisNexis) site is robots-disallowed and the docket system is robots/challenge-blocked. Justia opinion pages (Supreme Court from 1853, Courts of Appeal from 1897) are the readable text route, with slip pagination only. CCR: the official Westlaw host is blocked, and Cornell LII serves constructible CCR sections. Supreme Court weekly conference-result PDFs on supreme.courts.ca.gov are fetchable and give review grants and denials by docket number.

citation_map.notes: There is no public-domain citation format. California Style Manual cites put the year in parentheses before the volume and omit spaces ("69 Cal.2d 108"); Bluebook adds spaces ("69 Cal. 2d 108"). Docket prefixes: S = Supreme Court; A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H = Courts of Appeal Districts 1, 2, 3, 4/Div1, 4/Div2, 5, 4/Div3, 6. An M suffix marks a modification; an N suffix appears on archive file names. The courtlistener_id values come from memory and have not been checked against CourtListener. Routing caution: bare code names (Penal Code, Civil Code, Government Code) and bare 'rule N.N' are shared with other states and the federal rules; the regexes exclude Texas/Louisiana prefixes and 'of the Federal Rules', but route here only when the query or citation context is Californian.

access.pattern_rules: Section URLs follow /codes/california/code-{abbr}/{division-N}/{part-N}/.../section-{sec with dots as hyphens}/. The hierarchy segments cannot be derived from a citation.
access.navigation: From /codes/california/code-{abbr}/ (abbr = lower-case lawCode: civ, ccp, pen, …) follow whichever child link's section range contains the section — division, part, title, chapter, article, as present (the Penal Code starts at parts, not divisions) — until a page lists individual section links; then open the section.
